access_method: normal rendered OATD page in the dedicated local Chrome context; static direct HTTP returned 403 and was not used as evidence

observed_summary: The source describes itself as Open Access Theses and Dissertations and says it is a resource for finding open-access graduate theses and dissertations published around the world.

The rendered About section reported metadata from over 1,100 colleges, universities, and research institutions and displayed a current index-size figure. That display is an interface statement, not a frozen final-run total.
The page links to the contributing-sites list at https://oatd.org/oatd-publishers.html and to the FAQ.
OATD calls itself an index of over 7.3 million electronic theses and dissertations and says that, to the extent possible, it is limited to graduate-level records freely available online.
It says records come from contributing schools, their repositories, and some regional or national ETD consortia, mostly harvested with OAI-PMH.

It says full text lives on the original hosting site, usually the degree-granting university repository; OATD does not store the paper full text and indexes about the first 30 pages of some theses to show search hits.
It says it provides neither a bulk collection download nor an OAI-PMH metadata export.
It says source schools control record quality and full-text availability; changes or removals at an originating site are not necessarily reflected immediately.

Its PQDT comparison distinguishes the separate commercial ProQuest service: PQDT includes many but not all US dissertations, a smaller share of US master's theses, is institutionally restricted, and is primarily not open access.

boundary_conclusion.statement: For this protocol, use the full OATD index as one required indexed-online-resource event, not each linked institutional repository and not PQDT. The source documentation also establishes that OATD is a participating-repository/consortium aggregation with coverage, availability, currency, and metadata-quality limits; it is not evidence of complete global ETD coverage or of an individual work's completed degree status.
